articles.title: Extreme Heat Poses Greater Danger to Older Adults Than Previously Understood
articles.excerpt: New research shows heat-related mortality among people over 65 has surged by 85% since the early 2000s, with India's elderly population among the most vulnerable globally.
articles.image_caption: A person shielding from the sun during a heat wave. New research suggests extreme heat poses greater risks to older adults than previously understood.
articles.nri_angle: India is among the hardest-hit countries, with its elderly population facing severe risk from rising temperatures. Lost labor hours from heat exposure have cost India's economy billions annually.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ancient Galaxy Collision Transformed the Milky Way Billions of Years Ago, Studies Reveal
articles.excerpt: New research shows the Gaia-Sausage-Enceladus merger 11 billion years ago destroyed and rebuilt the Milky Way's disk, triggering an explosion of star formation.
articles.nri_angle: The research involves international collaboration including scientists from institutions worldwide, reflecting the kind of cross-border scientific work familiar to diaspora researchers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Stellantis Recalls Nearly One Million Vehicles Over Backup Camera Software Glitch
articles.excerpt: Radio software in 2026-27 Chrysler, Jeep, Dodge and Ram models may prevent rearview cameras from displaying properly; over-the-air fix is forthcoming.
articles.nri_angle: The recall affects popular models widely owned by Indian-American families across the United States, including the Chrysler Pacifica minivan and Jeep Grand Cherokee SUV.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Trump Hints at National Emergency to Force Voter ID Laws, Cites India's Election System as Model
articles.excerpt: With the SAVE America Act stalled in the Senate, the president declined to rule out using emergency powers to impose voter ID requirements ahead of the 2026 midterms, pointing to India's biometric voter verification as the standard.
articles.image_caption: President Donald Trump at the White House. Trump has cited India's biometric voter ID system as a model while pushing the SAVE America Act ahead of the 2026 midterm elections.
articles.nri_angle: Trump has repeatedly cited India's biometric voter ID system and Aadhaar as the gold standard for election reform, drawing India's election infrastructure into the center of the U.S. midterm debate.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Netanyahu Places NYC Mayor Mamdani on Tel Aviv Billboard Alongside Iran's Ayatollah and Hezbollah Chief
articles.excerpt: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's re-election campaign features Indian-American Mayor Zohran Mamdani alongside Iran's Supreme Leader and Hezbollah's chief with the message: 'They want Netanyahu to lose.'
articles.nri_angle: NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani is the city's first Indian-American mayor, son of Indian filmmaker Mira Nair and Ugandan-Indian academic Mahmood Mamdani, now featured in Israeli election campaign
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Traffic Deaths Surge 15% on Major Album Release Days, Harvard Study Finds
articles.excerpt: A new study published in JAMA Network Open links blockbuster album drops by Taylor Swift, Drake, and Bad Bunny to a sharp spike in fatal car crashes — with distracted smartphone use the likely culprit.
articles.nri_angle: Lead researcher Dr. Vishal Patel is an Indian-American physician at Harvard Medical School whose personal experience inspired this landmark distracted driving study
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Rights Group Urges FIFA to Block Infantino Re-Election Bid, Citing Term Limit Violation
articles.excerpt: FairSquare has filed a formal complaint arguing FIFA President Gianni Infantino has already served the maximum three terms, as mounting opposition threatens his decade-long grip on world football.
articles.nri_angle: Global football governance crisis with implications for the sport's direction worldwide
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Tyson Foods Shrinks Beef Operations as Historic Cattle Shortage Forces Industry-Wide Plant Closures
articles.excerpt: The nation's largest meat processor is closing multiple beef plants and expects up to $650 million in losses as U.S. cattle herds hit a 75-year low, with rivals JBS and Cargill also shuttering facilities.
articles.nri_angle: Major U.S. food industry restructuring affecting prices and supply chains relevant to diaspora consumers
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Inside Texas Republicans' Escalating Campaign Against Muslim Communities
articles.excerpt: From the governor's terrorist designations to convention delegates being told to leave the country, anti-Muslim rhetoric has become a central pillar of Texas GOP politics in 2026.
articles.nri_angle: Rising Islamophobia in Texas is affecting broader immigrant communities, with cities home to large Indian-origin populations also facing anti-immigrant protests.

articles.title: War and Drought Are Choking the World's Most Vital Trade Routes
articles.excerpt: From the Strait of Hormuz to the Red Sea and Black Sea, simultaneous disruptions at critical maritime chokepoints are driving up shipping costs and threatening global energy and food security.
articles.nri_angle: India is highly exposed as a major oil importer dependent on Hormuz transit, with Indian crew members killed in attacks and fertilizer supply chains for Indian agriculture disrupted.
